schema: alpha,d,kappa,Ps,ns,alpha_s (alpha-major, d, kappa-minor; 512000 rows; coordinates in data/grid_axes.json)

Ps.meaning: S_R = b^2 M_Pl^2 P_R = kappa^3/(2 pi^2) |u_hat/z|^2 at x_final (dimensionless)
Ps.row_status: all rows converged (every returned initial time passed the vacuum checks after the safety factor; none at the search cap)
Ps.code_hash_note: code_sha256_at_run are the hashes of the numerical modules' working-tree bytes at scan time. background.py hashes identically to the released LF file; modes.py at run had the same content with CRLF line endings (its scan-time hash equals the released content re-encoded with CRLF); spectra.py and table.py differ from their scan-time bytes in content, not only in line endings (table.py's command-line interface was extended after the run: derivatives subcommand and generated-axis options; the scan-time versions of both files are not in the repository, so the exact differences are not recoverable from it). Consequently the recorded checkpoint fingerprint (which includes table.py's hash) is not re-derivable from the released code, and byte identity between the released solver and the code that produced Ps is established for background.py and modes.py only. The released code reproduces the released Ps values bitwise at the 24 reserved grid points (tests/test_final_check_sample.py) and the regression fixture to 1e-9 (tests/test_regression_fixture.py).

code_hash_verification.spectra.py: CONTENT DIFFERS (modified after the scan; scan-time bytes not in the repository)
code_hash_verification.table.py: CONTENT DIFFERS (modified after the scan; scan-time bytes not in the repository)

derivatives.method: centred 7-point finite differences of ln Ps in ln kappa; 3 extra converged modes per side per (alpha,d); no smoothing

five_point_vs_seven_point.note: truncation-order consistency diagnostic on the same data

reproduction: python -m vcdm_genesis.table derivatives --amplitudes OUT/amplitudes.csv --workdir OUT/derivatives --output genesis_scan_table.csv --processes 18
hash_convention: SHA-256 values of text files are of LF-normalized bytes (equal to the committed Git blobs and to the release archive); a CRLF checkout on Windows yields different file hashes
